headline: Students threaten Education Ministry siege over HSC exam issues
summary: Protesters announce a 'Long March to the Education Ministry' after police used batons to disperse crowds near the Parliament area.
details: Students gathered near the National Parliament area to protest issues surrounding the HSC examinations.
Following a clash where police used batons to disperse the protesters, the students announced a 'Long March to the Education Ministry'.
The protesters left the Parliament area after making the announcement, signaling a shift in their target for the demonstration.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister's Advisor Mahdi Amin stated that a decision has been made to take student-friendly measures regarding the matter.
caption:
From the Parliament area to the Ministry: Students announce a 'Long March' after police clashes.

Students gathered near the National Parliament area to protest issues surrounding the HSC examinations.

Following a clash where police used batons to disperse the protesters, the students announced a 'Long March to the Education Ministry'.

The protesters left the Parliament area after making the announcement, signaling a shift in their target for the demonstration.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister's Advisor Mahdi Amin stated that a decision has been made to take student-friendly measures regarding the matter.

headline_marked: BB allows [[defaulting Shinepukur Ceramics to open LCs]] for raw materials
headline: BB allows defaulting Shinepukur Ceramics to open LCs for raw materials
summary: The central bank granted a special 18-month exemption to the Beximco Group company to sustain production and protect its workforce.
details: Bangladesh Bank has allowed Shinepukur Ceramics, a defaulting company of the Beximco Group, to open letters of credit (LCs) for raw material imports under a special arrangement.
The central bank stated the move is intended to keep production running at the ceramics manufacturer and protect the jobs of its workforce.
Under this arrangement, the company can open import LCs with Sonali Bank PLC by depositing a 100 percent margin, meaning the full import value must be paid in advance.
The move exempts Shinepukur Ceramics from Section 27 Ka Ka (3) of the Banking Companies Act, which normally bars banks from extending loan facilities to defaulting borrowers.
This exemption is valid for 18 months. As a condition, all revenue earned by the company must be deposited into a designated account for Sonali Bank to recover outstanding dues.

The government and central bank will not assume any responsibility for the loan facility provided for these LCs, and Sonali Bank cannot seek financial assistance from them for these loans in the future.
This follows a similar facility granted earlier this month to Abdul Monem Sugar Refinery Ltd, another defaulting borrower.
